prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: Researchers recorded activity from 1,415 neurons in neurosurgical patients who had just learned a story containing specific concepts.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study observed that neurons associated with the learned concepts became active again during slow-wave sleep following the learning task.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: These concept neurons fired together, especially during sharp-wave ripples, with timing gaps that could support changes in synaptic connections.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The order in which the neurons reactivated did not match the order of the concepts presented in the story.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Unlike rodent place cells that adjust their firing locations based on pre-existing sequences, human concept neurons are already tuned to specific meanings before any new learning occurs.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In contrast to rodent place cells, the reactivation of human concept cells does not mirror the sequence of events in human experiences.
facts.subject: humans
